newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable on client buying, position-squaring.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable on client buying, position-squaring.

text.p: The rouble was stable on Monday and dealers said its decline had been halted by bank client demand, attractive overnight credit rates and position-squaring after last week's government bond price rise.

"Some banks are seeking roubles because they are more attractive than dollar investments. Besides, rates are steady as there has been client (dollar) selling," Inkombank dealer Vladislav Savelyev said.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 40-60 percent compared with Friday's late 15-25 percent.
Konversbank dealer Stanislav Belov said rouble demand was higher also due to active T-bill and OFZ bond buying on Thursday and Friday, with banks currently closing short rouble positions.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,376-79 per dollar compared with an early 5,382-85 and 5,375-78 late on Friday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at 5,384-87 per dollar.
The central bank said it had set 5,353/5,393 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday.
